subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Mention the structures and names of the monomers used for preparing the following polymers: 1) Bakelite 2) Polystyrene 3) Teflon 4) Polyvinyl chloride 5) Nylon-6,6 6) Glyptal 7) Terylene 8) Buna-N.

mark_split.label: Monomers of the first four polymers
Monomers of the last four polymers

verification.note: Unit 12 (Polymers), printed as VSAQ 8 on book p.96. BOOK TABLE: the printed answer is an eight row table on book p.96 and its chemistry is correct throughout. Two things are tidied. First, the printed name "Tetrafluroethene" is misspelled; it is tetrafluoroethene. Second, the printed rings for phthalic and terephthalic acid are drawn with the two COOH groups in different positions but are never labelled 1,2- and 1,4-, which is the only difference between glyptal and terylene; the positions are stated here. The printed structure for ethylene glycol is drawn as two stacked CH₂–OH groups and is written linearly here as HO–CH₂–CH₂–OH. NOTE ON PAGE ORDER: the question is printed on book p.95 and the whole of book p.96 is its answer table, so book p.96 carries no question of its own; that is not a gap in the numbering.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Monomers of the first four polymers
lines: needs two and is a copolymer.
steps.why: The three single monomer polymers here all have a C=C double bond, so they add. Bakelite is different: it needs two monomers with different functional groups, so it condenses and releases water at every link.
common_mistakes: Writing the styrene formula as C₆H₅–CH₂–CH₃. Styrene must have the double bond, C₆H₅–CH=CH₂.
Writing tetrafluoroethene as CF₃–CF₃. It is CF₂=CF₂, with a double bond.
steps.memory_tip: Teflon is ethene with all four hydrogens replaced by fluorine; PVC is ethene with one replaced by chlorine.
steps.margin_note: Both the name and the structure are asked. A name with no formula is usually half of each item.

steps.label: Monomers of the last four polymers
steps.why: These four all need two monomers. Glyptal and terylene use the same alcohol and differ only in where the two –COOH groups are placed on the ring, so writing 1,2- and 1,4- is the only way to tell the two answers apart.
common_mistakes: Writing the same acid for glyptal and terylene. Glyptal uses phthalic acid, 1,2-, and terylene uses terephthalic acid, 1,4-.
Writing adipic acid as HOOC–(CH₂)₆–COOH. It has four –CH₂– groups; the diamine has six.
steps.memory_tip: Nylon-6,6 counts six carbons in each monomer: four –CH₂– plus two –COOH carbons in the acid, and six –CH₂– in the amine.
steps.margin_note: Eight polymers over two marks means four per mark. Number them so partial credit is easy to award.

insider_note: The pair most often confused is glyptal against terylene: same ethylene glycol, different benzene dicarboxylic acid. Write 1,2- and 1,4- and both items are correct.
